claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is SUPERSEDED.
In CodePipeline SUPERSEDED execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline SUPERSEDED mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it starts.
In SUPERSEDED mode, if a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
CodePipeline QUEUED execution mode makes waiting executions form a queue and each runs in turn.
CodePipeline QUEUED execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
Both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set when defining the pipeline, via the AWS CLI create-pipeline/update-pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that prevents concurrent deployment runs targeting that environment.
An exclusive lock check is added from the Azure DevOps environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` can be set on a stage that references an environment with an exclusive lock check.
The default value of Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has an `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource for managing the exclusive lock check as code.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ describing update conflicts.
The Pulumi@1 Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command`, `stack`, and `args`.

When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
The page links to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ as the update conflict page.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' under the configuration's General Settings, with a default of 0 (unlimited).
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 queues a second build behind the first, and it runs only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives the same one-at-a-time behavior as limiting TeamCity builds to 1.
In Azure Pipelines, serializing Pulumi deployments is done by adding an exclusive lock check to the environment the deployment job targets, together with `lockBehavior: sequential` on the stage.
`lockBehavior: sequential` is a valid Azure Pipelines stage-level setting that makes runs wait for the exclusive lock in sequence.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
AWS CodePipeline's execution mode can be set to `QUEUED` so that waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' that, set to 1, prevents concurrent builds.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
